title: Green flags, Valmiki edition

verse.sanskrit:
कथञ्चिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति ।
न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया ॥
verse.iast:
kathañcid upakāreṇa kṛtenaikena tuṣyati |
na smaraty apakārāṇāṃ śatam apy ātmavattayā ||
verse.translation: He is pleased by a single kindness, however it was done, and, being self-possessed, he does not remember even a hundred wrongs.

beats.title: VALMIKI EDITION
beats.vo: Valmiki literally wrote down Rama's green flags. And honestly? The bar is in heaven.
He speaks gently first. And even when someone's harsh to him, he doesn't clap back.
Do him one favour, he's happy. Do him a hundred wrongs? He's not keeping the receipts.
One kindness, and he's pleased. A hundred wrongs, and he doesn't even remember them.
Meanwhile us: still holding screenshots of an argument from 2019.

beats.title: Keep the kindness. Delete the grudges.
beats.vo: Not a doormat. Rama fought when it mattered. He just didn't let small stuff live rent free in his head.

beats.vo: Day two of learning from Rama. Send this to the friend who forgives too fast.

caption:
Rama's green flags, straight from Valmiki ✅

“कथञ्चिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया ॥”
He is pleased by a single kindness and does not remember even a hundred wrongs. (Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 1.11)

Keep the kindness. Delete the grudges.
